en.title: Fortnite's Latest Horror Collab Is Its Most Baffling Yet
en.summary: Fortnite's penchant for unexpected crossovers has reached a new peak with a bizarre collaboration tied to the indie horror film **Obsession**. The ad has left many fans scratching their heads, questioning the creative direction.
en.body:
## A Sprite's Obsession

**Fortnite** has built a reputation for its seemingly endless stream of collaborations, pulling in everything from Marvel superheroes to chart-topping musicians. The latest addition to this eclectic mix, however, has raised more than a few eyebrows: a promotional tie-in with the horror film **Obsession**. The one-minute ad, designed to promote both the film and the game, features a jarring shift from the movie's suspenseful narrative to a bizarre **Fortnite**-centric retelling. Instead of the film's female lead, Nikki, a rare **Galaxy Zero Point Sprite**—estimated to have a 1 in 300 million drop rate—becomes the object of obsession for the male protagonist, Bear. He replaces the film's wish-granting artifact with a "One Llama Luck" stick, causing the Sprite to become fixated on him.

This particular collaboration has proven divisive. For viewers unfamiliar with **Obsession**, the ad might appear as a quirky nod to **Fortnite**'s notoriously rare in-game items and the player base's dedication. However, for those who have seen the film, the ad takes on a deeply unsettling and potentially offensive tone. The source material, **Obsession**, deals with themes of control and autonomy, including references to sexual assault, making the playful, objectified portrayal of the Sprite—and its connection to the film's dark narrative—a questionable creative choice that seems to miss the mark.

## Community Questions the Crossover

The gaming community, particularly **Fortnite**'s dedicated fanbase, has responded with a mixture of confusion and criticism. While **Fortnite** has a history of embracing diverse IPs, this latest venture feels particularly out of left field. The success of **Fortnite** in 2026, with ongoing collaborations like **South Park** and **One Piece**, has shown Epic Games' commitment to keeping the game fresh. However, the **Obsession** ad has ignited discussions about whether *every* popular piece of media warrants a **Fortnite** crossover, especially when the thematic connections are tenuous or, in this case, potentially problematic. Many fans took to platforms like Reddit to express their bewilderment, questioning the decision-making process behind such a partnership and its perceived insensitivity.

## What's Next for Fortnite Collaborations?

As **Fortnite** continues its aggressive collaboration strategy into 2026, with rumors of more partnerships with franchises like Universal and potential mini-passes, the **Obsession** ad serves as a stark reminder of the fine line between innovative marketing and misjudged execution. Future collaborations will undoubtedly be watched closely by a community eager for exciting content but wary of ventures that feel forced or disrespectful to source material. Details on upcoming **Fortnite** updates and partnerships are expected to be revealed throughout the year.

content_raw: Honestly, I thought I could no longer be surprised by the off-the-wall collaborations between Fortnite and various other IPs. At this point in Fortnite's very lucrative lifespan, the general rule of thumb seems to be, "If it's popular, it's gonna end up in Fortnite." Damn near every Marvel Cinematic Universe character has made an appearance, countless musical artists have held in-game concerts, and Epic has always been very good at making sure that whatever the internet is obsessed with at any given moment ends up tied to the game in one way or another. The problem is that the internet is currently obsessed with Curry Barker's wildly successful horror film, Obsession . Epic Games and Blumhouse Productions apparently thought this would be a good time to release a collaborative ad for both Fortnite and Barker's film, which just hit streaming services after an extended theatrical run . The one-minute ad features various "jump-scare" moments from Obsession, but replaces the film's female lead, Nikki (Inde Navarrette), with a Galaxy Zero Point Sprite (the rarest collectible Sprite in Fortnite, with a drop rate of roughly 1 in 300 million). Instead of using a One Wish Willow as he did in the film, main character Bear (Michael Johnston) is shown snapping a "One Llama Luck" stick in half, causing the Sprite to become obsessed with him. Editor's note: The following includes major spoilers for Obsession, and also contains references to sexual assault. If you haven't seen the film, the video reads as a silly little nod to how obsessed Fortnite players are with the extremely rare Sprite. If you have seen the film, this entire ad spot is baffling at best and offensive at worst. In Obsession, Nikki loses her autonomy after Bear wishes that Nikki "loved [him] more than anyone in the f***ing world." Bear gets his wish, but it quickly becomes apparent that the real Nikki is trapped inside her body, unable to control it as she has been possessed by whatever magic lies within the One Wish Willow. Even after it becomes painfully clear that the version of Nikki that "loves" him isn't the real Nikki, Bear continues to act as if she is his girlfriend, repeatedly raping her and pretending they have a normal relationship, despite the fact that the real Nikki occasionally claws her way to the surface and begs him to free her. In short, Bear is the villain, but he's not the sort of villain the audience is meant to like or relate to. He is dangerously obsessive, dishonest, and manipulative, and consistently makes the most selfish move every time he's presented with a choice. He's also, y'know, a rapist. Obsession's "twist" is the fact that, despite her horrific behavior while possessed, Nikki is the victim , and Bear is the aggressor. By the time the film ends, Nikki has regained her autonomy but is all alone, surrounded by the corpses of the people she once called friends--one of whom turned out to be a rapist, and two of whom Nikki killed against her will while possessed.
